Microsoft just built its own frontier AI model.

8 trillion parameters. Zero distillation from any external model. And according to Microsoft leadership, it already beats the base model powering GPT 5.6 Soul — before fine-tuning even starts.

This changes the competitive map of AI. For years, Microsoft funded OpenAI while relying on its models. That era is ending. Microsoft is now a direct frontier model competitor alongside Google, Anthropic, and a handful of others.

What does this mean for business leaders? The AI model layer is consolidating fast. Only companies with massive compute budgets can compete at this scale. The real differentiation for everyone else moves to how you deploy, orchestrate, and specialize AI — not which base model you use.

For CTOs evaluating vendor lock-in, this is the moment to stress-test your AI architecture. For CEOs, the strategic question is clear: when every major cloud provider ships a world-class model, what makes your AI investment defensible?
